messages.subject: Maps and adding overlays
parts:
I would like to use ggplot to produce annotated maps e.g.
library(mapproj)

world <-data.frame(map("world", plot=FALSE)[c("x","y")])

## default graphics
plot(world$x,world$y,type="l")
points((-5:5)*10,(-5:5)*10,pch=19,cex=(1:11)/2)

But because the overlay has a different number of points from the map
it fails

## ggplot
worldMap <-ggplot(world) + geom_path(aes(x,y))
worldMap+geom_point(aes(x=(-5:5)*10,y=(-5:5)*10))

Is there an easy way to do this.


Laurie

messages.author: fec9673bf72eb326
messages.subject: Re: Maps and adding overlays
parts:
Laurie,

I think this should do what you want:

pointData <- data.frame(xx=(-5:5)*10,yy=(-5:5)*10,zz=(1:11)/2)

worldMap <-ggplot(world) + geom_path(aes(x,y))
worldMap+geom_point(data=pointData,aes(x=xx,y=yy,size=zz))

Dave

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Maps and adding overlays
parts:
Hi:

Here's one approach:

First, assign the point coordinates to a data frame:
pts <- data.frame(x = (-5:5) * 10, y = (-5:5) * 10)

# Plot 1: Legend present
worldMap + geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y, size = 1:11)) +
    scale_size("Size")

# Plot 2: Legend absent
worldMap + geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y, size = 1:11)) +
   scale_size(legend = FALSE)

There are many ways to play with the legend if you choose to keep it. One way
would be to add the point size as a new column in pts, assign it as a(n ordered)
factor, and repeat plot 1.

HTH,
Dennis
